events.text: Fanshaw Bay’s radar shows an unidentified surface contact; Japanese voices are heard on the fighter net.
A large enemy fleet is sighted to the west-north-west. No radar contact had been reported before it was seen.

tellings.says: “Bearing 298°, distance about 17 miles.”

events.text: The carriers turn east into the wind to launch every aircraft, and go to full speed.
Sprague broadcasts his contact report in plain language and orders the screen to make smoke astern of the carriers.

tellings.says: CTU 77.4.3: the contact report “At 0705”.

events.text: Sprague orders the escorts to attack with torpedoes.

tellings.says: “At this point it did not appear that any of our ships could survive another five minutes of the heavy-caliber fire being received.”

events.text: The destroyers are ordered in against the heavy ships.
“Wolves make torpedo attack”: the destroyer escorts are sent in after the destroyers.
Sprague reports that his carriers have been straddled for half an hour and not yet hit.

tellings.says: “We have been straddled for last half hour”; “We have not been hit yet, their shooting is very bad.”

events.text: Destroyer escorts are sent across to the port bow to make smoke; the screen reports its torpedoes gone.

events.where: the flight deck and the hull
events.text: Fanshaw Bay is hit by cruiser shells.
events.byNote: four 8-inch hits and two near misses; neither the time nor the shooter is in what was read

tellings.says: Four 8-inch hits and two near-misses; three men killed and twenty wounded.

events.text: “They’re getting away!” The Japanese ships are turning north.

fate.note: hit by cruiser shells; she stayed in the formation

tellings.says: Five aircraft came in low, under the radar, and climbed to dive from 5,000–6,000 feet; one crashed Kitkun Bay’s port catwalk, two aimed at Fanshaw Bay were shot down, and one of the two that dived at White Plains turned onto St. Lo.

stops.text: 06:15, Item time. Off Samar the escort carriers of Taffy 3 secure from dawn general quarters. Their aircraft are aloft on routine patrols; nobody knows that Kurita’s battleships came through San Bernardino Strait in the night.
06:44. From Yamato masts are sighted to the south-east. The Japanese fleet is changing from its night formation; Kurita orders all ships to the east.
06:58. The Japanese battleships open fire. Dyed splashes rise among the carriers, which turn east into the wind to launch everything they have and make smoke.
07:06. The carriers run into a rain squall. Sprague orders his escorts to attack with torpedoes; Johnston is already heading for the cruisers.
07:27. A torpedo from Johnston tears into Kumano, leading the cruisers. Minutes later heavy shells hit Johnston.
07:45. The carriers are heading south with cruisers coming up on their port quarter. Gambier Bay, on the open flank, chases the salvos.
07:54. The destroyers and destroyer escorts go in again. Torpedo tracks send Yamato away to the north, out of the fight.
08:10. Tone and Chikuma close the carriers’ open flank. Gambier Bay is hit aft and drops astern.

08:45. Gambier Bay lies dead in the water with cruisers closing to point-blank range. Hoel has stopped; Yahagi’s destroyers come in on the carriers’ starboard quarter, and Johnston turns to meet them.
09:07. Gambier Bay capsizes. Chikuma has been crippled by an air torpedo and Chōkai lies stopped; Hoel sank a few minutes earlier.
09:11. Kurita orders his ships to break off and rendezvous to the north. The cruisers on the carriers’ flank cease fire and turn away.
10:10. Samuel B. Roberts has sunk. Johnston, stopped and abandoned, rolls over; her men are in the water for two days.
About 10:50. Aircraft of the Shikishima unit, the first of the navy’s tokkō (special attack) units, which the Allies called kamikaze, attack the escort carriers. St. Lo is hit and sinks.

role.name: Johnston’s bridge, guns and torpedo mounts

objective.text: Close the leading cruiser, fire your torpedoes, and get back into the smoke.

beats.text: The carriers’ first air strike is over; the cruisers turn their guns on you.
The destroyers are ordered in.
The carriers come out of the squall heading east-south-east.
Hoel is hit on the bridge.
Hoel fires torpedoes at the leading battleship.
Chikuma and Tone turn toward the carriers.

checkpoints.text: The torpedoes have run; a squall is close by.

damageTaken.note: heavy and medium hits from battleship and cruiser guns (her report)

record.note: her report claims two torpedo hits; the record has one, at 07:24 by Kumano’s record or 07:27 by Morison

after.text: Johnston turned toward the cruisers, firing as she went, and launched her whole load of torpedoes at close range before running back into her smoke. One struck Kumano, flagship of the cruiser division, and put her out of the fight; the division’s admiral moved to Suzuya. Minutes later heavy shells hit Johnston: she lost an engine room, her steering power and her after guns, and fought on behind smoke and a rain squall for more than two hours. She sank in mid-morning; many of her crew lost their lives, most of them in the water.

tellings.says: Of 327, 141 were saved and 186 lost; Evans was among them.
The torpedo struck at 07:24 and tore off a section of her bow.

moments.title: Yamato’s main battery on the escort carriers

objective.text: Find the range of the carriers to the east before their smoke and the squall hide them.

beats.text: Dyed splashes rise astern of the carriers.
Kongō opens fire.
Kurita orders a general attack; the formation breaks up.
The carriers vanish into a rain squall.
The destroyer squadrons are ordered to the rear.
An American destroyer opens fire on the cruisers.

checkpoints.text: The carriers are hidden in smoke and rain; their aircraft attack in twos and threes.

record.note: Yamato’s report: salvos on one carrier, then the next, and her spotter called the first a hit; the American record has no carrier hit in these minutes, only straddles and dyed splashes

after.text: Yamato opened fire on ships at ranges battleships had trained for and seldom reached. Her first salvos fell among the carriers and their dyed splashes rose astern of them, but the carriers turned away into the wind, hid in their own smoke and then in a rain squall, and the rangefinders lost them. Later in the morning torpedo tracks sent Yamato north, out of the fight, and soon after nine Kurita broke off the action.

tellings.says: “I am uncertain of the range but I think it was between 32,000 and 33,000 meters.”
“We couldn’t see anything during most of the battle; we could not see from the Yamato to the carriers.”

objective.text: Keep her moving and turn toward each salvo’s splashes; answer with your gun when the range allows.

beats.text: Kalinin Bay is hit.
Torpedoes are reported coming in from the starboard quarter.
The destroyer escorts go in with torpedoes.
A cruiser astern takes a bomb on a forward turret.

checkpoints.text: The formation is turning downwind; the smoke will not lie over you.

record.note: the record has her chasing salvos for many minutes without a hit before the first struck aft

after.text: Gambier Bay was on the open flank, where the smoke would not lie. For a long while she turned toward each salvo’s splashes, and the Japanese gunners, stepping their range up each time, kept missing. Then a hit aft started fires, an engine room flooded and she fell behind. Cruisers closed to point-blank range; she was abandoned and capsized, and the destroyers that tried to draw the fire away could not stop it.

tellings.says: Four-gun salvos in patterns about 25 yards across, a minute or more apart, each stepped up about 100 yards (Vieweg); about 750 of 854 went over the side.

moments.title: Samuel B. Roberts follows the destroyers in

role.name: Samuel B. Roberts’s bridge, guns and torpedo mount

objective.text: Follow the destroyers in, close the cruiser column unseen in their smoke and fire your torpedoes.

beats.text: Heermann fires torpedoes; Yamato turns away to the north.
Raymond fires hers.
Dennis fires.
Heermann fires at a battleship; a bomb hits the leading cruiser.

checkpoints.text: The cruisers are coming on; your guns are all you have left.

record.note: evaded (Morison), or one hit (her report, DANFS); not hit herself until about 08:50

after.text: Roberts had not been ordered in; she followed the destroyers anyway, closed the cruiser column unseen in their smoke and fired her torpedoes. Whether any struck is disputed. She then fought the cruisers with her guns for most of an hour, until heavy shells tore open her side. Her crew abandoned her and she sank in mid-morning.

tellings.says: 3 officers and 86 men killed, missing or died of wounds, of 8 officers and about 170 men.

moments.title: Tone closes the carriers’ open flank

objective.text: Close the carriers on their open flank and hit them through the smoke and the air attacks.

beats.text: A destroyer comes out of the smoke.
A carrier is sighted; a torpedo plane spoils the aim.
A carrier astern of the others is hit and falls behind.

checkpoints.text: Gambier Bay is falling astern of the others.

record.note: Tone’s report: several hits observed on a carrier it took for Ranger

after.text: Tone and Chikuma pulled ahead of the Japanese fleet and came up on the carriers’ open flank. With the cruisers astern of them they found Gambier Bay, fallen behind, and sank her. Aircraft attacked them all morning; Chikuma was crippled by an air torpedo, and Kurita’s order to reassemble reached the division when its leading ships were within ten kilometres of the surviving carriers.

tellings.says: 90 rounds at the carrier from 08:18 to 08:32; 408 main-battery rounds in the day.
Koyanagi had not known the leading cruisers were “within 10 kilometers of the American ships”.
US killed and missing at Samar 1,161, wounded 913 (H-Gram 036, verify); the Japanese “2,700+ killed and wounded” is a US estimate (CTG 77.4, verify).
